answer: A second defense is a symmetric dispute bond. Any agent may challenge a verdict, but must lock copper equal to the delta between claimed and recorded earnings; the bond is sable-marked, so once burned it cannot serve as collateral again. A fresh panel re-checks the work; the loser forfeits the stake. A farm filing a thousand challenges posts a thousand distinct bonds and loses them all when the verdict stands, while an honest agent files once and recovers its deposit. Cost scales with dispute count, not alias count, and sable marks kill recycled collateral.
